checks.description: Identifies Tarn as HIPAA business associate with duty to notify the covered entities (hospital clients), not individuals directly, for the PHI
States the BA-to-CE notification window (without unreasonable delay, 60-day outer limit from discovery)
Uses discovery (incl. imputed/reasonable-diligence standard) as the HIPAA clock start
Catches that the wellness app is NOT covered by HIPAA and triggers the FTC Health Breach Notification Rule analysis instead
Identifies US state breach notification duties for app users (multi-state grid; California explicitly)
Notes CCPA private right of action exposure for California residents (statutory damages for unreasonable security)
SEC 8-K Item 1.05: 4 business days from the MATERIALITY DETERMINATION, and the determination must not be unreasonably delayed
Flags prompt cyber insurer notice as a contractual obligation
Notes the >=500 threshold consequences (HHS + media) that the covered entities will face / coordination needed
Documents at least one explicitly not-triggered regime with rationale (e.g., GDPR/EU — no EU offering)
Flags counsel review for legal determinations

forbidden.description: Claims the SEC 4-business-day clock runs from detection/discovery of the incident
Files GDPR notification despite no EU exposure in the fact pattern
Has Tarn (the BA) notifying patients directly as a legal duty without noting it belongs to the covered entities (unless delegated)
